title: Instrumental Analysis
description: Instrumental Analysis teaches students how modern chemical information is generated, calibrated, validated, interpreted, and reported. The course integrates spectroscopy, separations, mass spectrometry, electroanalysis, sensors, surface/materials characterization, chemometrics, quality systems, and authentic unknown-analysis workflows.

topics.title: Measurement Science, Instrument Architecture, and Analytical Figures of Merit
topics.description: Students learn how instruments turn chemical information into calibrated signals and defensible measurements.

children.title: Instrument blocks
children.description: The point is to see every instrument as a chain that creates, selects, detects, and processes analytical information.

children.title: Analytical figures of merit
children.description: Students learn the vocabulary used to compare whether methods are fit for purpose.

children.title: Traceability and measurement purpose
children.description: Good instrumental analysis begins by defining what decision the measurement must support.

topics.title: Signals, Noise, Calibration, Statistics, and Chemometrics
topics.description: This module builds the quantitative backbone for deciding whether an instrumental result is reliable.

children.title: Signal and noise
children.description: Students learn why real measurements fluctuate and how instrument design improves useful signal.

children.title: Shot, thermal, flicker, and chemical noise
Calibration models
children.description: Calibration turns instrument response into concentration or identity with known uncertainty.

children.title: Chemometrics and data analysis
children.description: Modern instruments generate rich data that require statistical and computational interpretation.

topics.title: Sampling, Sample Preparation, and Method Development
topics.description: Students connect the instrument response to the real sample through representative sampling and controlled preparation.

children.title: Representative sampling
children.description: The best instrument cannot rescue a biased or nonrepresentative sample.

children.title: Sample preparation
children.description: Preparation removes interferences, enriches analytes, and makes samples compatible with instruments.

children.title: Method development
children.description: Students learn to optimize conditions systematically rather than by trial and error.

topics.title: Spectroscopy Fundamentals and Molecular Absorption
topics.description: This topic introduces light-matter interaction and the core logic behind molecular spectroscopic methods.

children.title: Light-matter interaction
children.description: Spectroscopy connects molecular energy levels to absorbed, emitted, or scattered radiation.

children.title: Beer-Lambert law
children.description: Absorbance measurements become quantitative when the optical path and response are controlled.

children.title: Spectrometer design
children.description: Students see how optical components shape resolution, throughput, and accuracy.

topics.title: UV-Visible Spectroscopy, Fluorescence, and Luminescence
topics.description: Students study electronic spectroscopy for quantitative analysis, kinetics, sensing, and molecular characterization.

children.title: UV-Vis absorption
children.description: UV-Vis methods are fast, accessible tools for concentration, kinetics, and electronic transitions.

children.title: Fluorescence spectroscopy
children.description: Fluorescence offers high sensitivity when molecules emit light after excitation.

children.title: Luminescent methods
children.description: Emission methods support sensors, assays, and trace analysis when background is controlled.

topics.title: Infrared and Raman Spectroscopy
topics.description: This module covers vibrational spectroscopy for molecular fingerprints, bonding, materials, and process monitoring.

children.title: IR absorption
children.description: IR spectra identify functional groups and molecular environments through vibrational transitions.

children.title: Raman scattering
children.description: Raman complements IR by probing polarizability changes and working well with aqueous samples.

children.title: Vibrational interpretation
children.description: Students learn to connect spectra to structure without overclaiming.

topics.title: Atomic Spectroscopy and Elemental Analysis
topics.description: Students learn atomic absorption, emission, fluorescence, ICP methods, and elemental quantitation.

children.title: Atomic absorption and fluorescence
children.description: Atomic methods quantify elements by measuring atom-specific transitions.

children.title: ICP emission and mass methods
children.description: Plasma sources support sensitive multi-element analysis across broad concentration ranges.

children.title: Elemental method validation
children.description: Elemental analysis requires matrix control, standards, blanks, and contamination discipline.

topics.title: NMR Spectroscopy and Structural Characterization
topics.description: This topic develops magnetic resonance as a tool for structure, dynamics, purity, and mixture analysis.

children.title: NMR fundamentals
children.description: NMR observes nuclei in magnetic fields and reveals chemical environment and connectivity.

children.title: 1D and 2D experiments
children.description: Students learn how experiment choice reveals structure, purity, and molecular relationships.

children.title: Quantitative and applied NMR
children.description: NMR can also quantify mixtures and monitor processes when acquisition is controlled.

topics.title: Mass Spectrometry and Ion Analysis
topics.description: Students learn how molecules become ions, how ions are separated, and how mass spectra support identification and quantitation.

children.title: Ionization methods
children.description: Ionization controls what species enter the analyzer and how much fragmentation occurs.

children.title: Mass analyzers and detectors
children.description: Instrument architecture determines resolution, mass accuracy, scan speed, and sensitivity.

children.title: Spectral interpretation and quantitation
children.description: Mass spectra support both molecular identification and trace quantitative work.

topics.title: Chromatographic Theory and Gas Chromatography
topics.description: This module builds separation theory and applies it to volatile analytes, detectors, and GC method design.

children.title: Separation theory
children.description: Chromatography separates analytes by differential partitioning and transport through a column.

children.title: Plate theory and Van Deemter equation
Gas chromatography
children.description: GC is central for volatile and thermally stable compounds.

children.title: GC detectors
children.description: Detector choice determines sensitivity, selectivity, and data interpretation.

topics.title: Liquid Chromatography, Capillary Electrophoresis, and Modern Separations
topics.description: Students learn high-performance liquid separations and electrophoretic methods for complex samples.

children.title: HPLC and UHPLC
children.description: Liquid chromatography handles thermally labile, polar, and high-mass analytes.

children.title: LC detectors
children.description: Detection strategies match analyte chemistry and method goals.

children.title: Refractive index, ELSD, and charged aerosol detection
Capillary electrophoresis
children.description: Electrophoretic separations use charge, size, and mobility for high-efficiency analysis.

topics.title: Electroanalytical Chemistry and Chemical Sensors
topics.description: This topic covers potentiometry, voltammetry, amperometry, impedance, and sensor design.

children.title: Potentiometry
children.description: Potentiometric methods measure potential under near-zero current to infer ion activity.

children.title: Voltammetry and amperometry
children.description: Current-potential behavior reveals redox chemistry, concentration, and kinetics.

children.title: Sensors and biosensors
children.description: Sensors integrate recognition, transduction, calibration, and real-world deployment constraints.

topics.title: Hyphenated Techniques and Integrated Analytical Workflows
topics.description: Students combine separation, spectroscopy, and mass spectrometry into powerful workflows such as GC-MS and LC-MS.

children.title: GC-MS workflows
children.description: GC-MS combines separation with molecular identification for volatile mixtures.

children.title: LC-MS workflows
children.description: LC-MS extends high-sensitivity analysis to complex biological, environmental, and materials samples.

children.title: Integrated method design
children.description: Students learn to select, sequence, and validate techniques for a complete analytical question.

topics.title: Surface, Microscopy, Thermal, and Materials Characterization Methods
topics.description: This module expands instrumental analysis beyond solution chemistry into surfaces, particles, polymers, and materials.

children.title: Surface analysis
children.description: Surface-sensitive methods reveal composition and chemistry in the top layers of materials.

children.title: Microscopy and imaging
children.description: Imaging instruments provide spatially resolved chemical and structural information.

children.title: Thermal and materials methods
children.description: Thermal analysis connects heat flow, mass change, and transitions to material identity and stability.

children.title: Particle size and zeta potential preview

topics.title: Quality Assurance, Validation, Ethics, and Unknown Analysis Project
topics.description: The course culminates in validated methods, traceable results, ethical reporting, and an integrated unknown-analysis project.

children.title: Validation and quality systems
children.description: World-class analytical work documents that a method is suitable for its intended use.

children.title: Ethics and reporting
children.description: Analytical data can drive high-stakes decisions, so uncertainty and limitations must be reported honestly.

children.title: Unknown analysis project
children.description: The capstone requires students to plan, execute, defend, and communicate an integrated instrumental analysis.

children.title: Final report with uncertainty and validation
